title: 上邪
author: 佚名（汉乐府）
intro: A woman swears to Heaven that she will love her man until mountains are worn flat, rivers run dry, thunder roars in winter and snow falls in summer. Only 35 characters long — and one of the boldest love vows in Chinese poetry.
analysis: 这是一个女子对爱人发下的誓言。开头一声“上邪！”——“天啊！”——就像对着老天大喊，请老天作证。她说：我要和你相爱，让这份爱永远不断、不减。接着她一口气列出五件不可能发生的事：高山变平，江水干了，冬天打雷，夏天下雪，天和地合在一起。只有这些事都发生了，她才敢和爱人分开。用“不可能的事”来表示“永远不会”，比直接说“我永远爱你”有力得多。句子长短不齐，有三个字的，也有七个字的，读起来像一口气说出来的话，感情又急又真。这首诗来自民间，语言大胆直白，和文人诗的含蓄很不一样，今天还常被用来表达忠贞不渝的爱情。
analysisEn: This is a vow of love, spoken by a woman to the man she loves. It opens with a cry — 上邪！ “O Heaven above!” — as if she is calling Heaven to be her witness. She says: I want to love you, and let this love last forever, never fading, never broken. Then, in one breath, she lists five things that can never happen: the mountains worn flat, the rivers run dry, thunder in winter, snow in summer, heaven and earth crashing together. Only when all of these happen would she dare to part from him. Saying “never” through a list of impossible things is far stronger than simply saying “I will love you forever.” The lines are uneven — some three characters long, some seven — so the poem sounds like real speech pouring out, urgent and sincere. As a folk song, it is bold and direct, very different from the restrained style of most poetry by scholars. It is still quoted today as a symbol of unshakeable, faithful love.
background: This anonymous song is one of the eighteen “Songs for Cymbals and Drums” (铙歌十八曲), a group of Han dynasty yuefu songs, preserved in Guo Maoqian’s Collection of Yuefu Poems (12th century). It is usually read as the vow of a young woman.
pronunciation: 上邪的“邪”读 yé（语气词，同“耶”，不读 xié）；夏雨雪的“雨”作动词“下”，读 yù；江水为竭的“为”读 wéi；相知的“相”读 xiāng。长命无绝衰的“衰”通行读本注 shuāi，旧读 cuī；此处采用 shuāi。
version: 采用通行文本（出自宋郭茂倩《乐府诗集·鼓吹曲辞·汉铙歌》），全诗九句、三十五字，长短句交错，网站按语意分为五行。

lines.zh: 我欲与君相知，长命无绝衰。
lines.rhythm: 我欲/与君/相知，长命/无绝衰
lines.py: wǒ yù yǔ jūn xiāng zhī, cháng mìng wú jué shuāi
lines.lit: I wish to love you, and let it last forever, never ending or fading.
lines.en: I want to love you, and let this love live forever — never fading, never broken.

lines.py: shān wú líng, jiāng shuǐ wéi jié
lines.lit: When the mountains have no peaks, when the rivers dry up,
lines.en: Not until the mountains are worn flat, not until the rivers run dry,

lines.py: dōng léi zhèn zhèn, xià yù xuě
lines.lit: when winter thunder rumbles, when it snows in summer,
lines.en: not until thunder roars in winter and snow falls in summer,

lines.py: tiān dì hé, nǎi gǎn yǔ jūn jué
lines.lit: when heaven and earth merge — only then would I dare to break with you!
lines.en: not until heaven and earth crash together — only then would I dare to leave you!

words.note: 同“耶”，读 yé。今天“邪”读 xié，指不正当，如“邪恶”。
现代汉语说“想”，“欲望”“欲言又止”里还保留。
古代对人的尊称，今天说“你”“您”。

words.en: to know and love each other
words.note: 今天“相知”多指互相了解的知心朋友。
今天“长命百岁”是祝人长寿。
现代汉语“丘陵”，也指帝王的墓，如“十三陵”。

words.en: to dry up; to be used up
words.note: 现代汉语“枯竭”“竭尽全力”。
现代汉语“合并”“合在一起”。

imagery.name: 山
imagery.zh: 高山被磨平——第一件不可能的事，表示爱情像山一样不会改变。
imagery.en: Mountains worn flat — the first impossible thing; her love is as unmoving as a mountain.

imagery.name: 江
imagery.zh: 江水干涸——江河永远在流，就像她的爱永远不断。
imagery.en: Rivers run dry — but rivers never stop flowing, just as her love never stops.

imagery.name: 雷
imagery.zh: 冬天打雷，违背自然规律，用来说明分手根本不可能。
imagery.en: Thunder in winter goes against nature — that is how impossible parting is.

imagery.name: 雪
imagery.zh: 夏天下雪，同样是不可能的事。
imagery.en: Snow in summer: another thing that can never happen.

imagery.name: 天地
imagery.zh: 天地合在一起是世界末日，只有那时她才会离开。
imagery.en: Heaven and earth crashing together means the end of the world — only then would she leave.
